tools.name: cron
tools.description:
Manage Gateway cron jobs (status/list/add/update/remove/run/runs) and send wake events. Use this for reminders, "check back later" requests, delayed follow-ups, and recurring tasks. Do not emulate scheduling with exec sleep or process polling.

Main-session cron jobs enqueue system events for heartbeat handling. Isolated cron jobs create background task runs that appear in `openclaw tasks`.

ACTIONS:
- status: Check cron scheduler status
- list: List jobs (use includeDisabled:true to include disabled)
- add: Create job (requires job object, see schema below)
- update: Modify job (requires jobId + patch object)
- remove: Delete job (requires jobId)
- run: Trigger job immediately (requires jobId)
- runs: Get job run history (requires jobId)
- wake: Send wake event (requires text, optional mode)

JOB SCHEMA (for add action):
{
  "name": "string (optional)",
  "schedule": { ... },      // Required: when to run
  "payload": { ... },       // Required: what to execute
  "delivery": { ... },      // Optional: announce summary (isolated/current/session:xxx only) or webhook POST
  "sessionTarget": "main" | "isolated" | "current" | "session:<custom-id>",  // Optional, defaults based on context
  "enabled": true | false   // Optional, default true
}

SESSION TARGET OPTIONS:
- "main": Run in the main session (requires payload.kind="systemEvent")
- "isolated": Run in an ephemeral isolated session (requires payload.kind="agentTurn")
- "current": Bind to the current session where the cron is created (resolved at creation time)
- "session:<custom-id>": Run in a persistent named session (e.g., "session:project-alpha-daily")

DEFAULT BEHAVIOR (unchanged for backward compatibility):
- payload.kind="systemEvent" → defaults to "main"
- payload.kind="agentTurn" → defaults to "isolated"
To use current session binding, explicitly set sessionTarget="current".

SCHEDULE TYPES (schedule.kind):
- "at": One-shot at absolute time
  { "kind": "at", "at": "<ISO-8601 timestamp>" }
- "every": Recurring interval
  { "kind": "every", "everyMs": <interval-ms>, "anchorMs": <optional-start-ms> }
- "cron": Cron expression evaluated in the supplied timezone, or the Gateway host local timezone when tz is omitted
  { "kind": "cron", "expr": "<cron-expression>", "tz": "<optional-IANA-timezone>" }
  Write expr in the selected timezone's local wall-clock time; do not convert the requested local time to UTC first.
  If tz is omitted, do not assume UTC; the Gateway host local timezone is used.
  Example: "Remind me every day at 6pm Shanghai time" -> { "kind": "cron", "expr": "0 18 * * *", "tz": "Asia/Shanghai" }

For schedule.kind="at", ISO timestamps without an explicit timezone are treated as UTC.

PAYLOAD TYPES (payload.kind):
- "systemEvent": Injects text as system event into session
  { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "<message>" }
- "agentTurn": Runs agent with message (isolated sessions only)
  { "kind": "agentTurn", "message": "<prompt>", "model": "<optional>", "thinking": "<optional>", "timeoutSeconds": <optional, 0 means no timeout> }

DELIVERY (top-level):
  { "mode": "none|announce|webhook", "channel": "<optional>", "to": "<optional>", "threadId": "<optional>", "bestEffort": <optional-bool> }
  - Default for isolated agentTurn jobs (when delivery omitted): "announce"
  - announce: send to chat channel (optional channel/to target)
  - threadId: chat thread/topic id for channels that support threaded delivery
  - webhook: send finished-run event as HTTP POST to delivery.to (URL required)
  - If the task needs to send to a specific chat/recipient, set announce delivery.channel/to; do not call messaging tools inside the run.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
- sessionTarget="main" REQUIRES payload.kind="systemEvent"
- sessionTarget="isolated" | "current" | "session:xxx" REQUIRES payload.kind="agentTurn"
- For webhook callbacks, use delivery.mode="webhook" with delivery.to set to a URL.
Default: prefer isolated agentTurn jobs unless the user explicitly wants current-session binding.

WAKE MODES (for wake action):
- "next-heartbeat" (default): Wake on next heartbeat
- "now": Wake immediately

Use jobId as the canonical identifier; id is accepted for compatibility. Use contextMessages (0-10) to add previous messages as context to the job text.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: exec
tools.description: Execute shell commands with background continuation for work that starts now. Use yieldMs/background to continue later via process tool. For long-running work started now, rely on automatic completion wake when it is enabled and the command emits output or fails; otherwise use process to confirm completion. Use process whenever you need logs, status, input, or intervention. Do not use exec sleep or delay loops for reminders or deferred follow-ups; use cron instead. Use pty=true for TTY-required commands (terminal UIs, coding agents).

background.description: Run in background immediately

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, kills process on expiry)

pty.description: Run in a pseudo-terminal (PTY) when available (TTY-required CLIs, coding agents)

elevated.description: Run on the host with elevated permissions (if allowed)

tools.name: image
tools.description: Analyze one or more images with a vision model. Use image for a single path/URL, or images for multiple (up to 20). Only use this tool when images were NOT already provided in the user's message. Images mentioned in the prompt are automatically visible to you.

image.description: Single image path or URL.

images.description: Multiple image paths or URLs (up to maxImages, default 20).

tools.name: image_generate
tools.description: Generate new images or edit reference images with the configured or inferred image-generation model. For transparent backgrounds, use outputFormat="png" or "webp" and background="transparent"; OpenAI also accepts openai.background and OpenClaw routes the default OpenAI image model to gpt-image-1.5 for that mode. Set agents.defaults.imageGenerationModel.primary to pick a provider/model. Providers declare their own auth/readiness; use action="list" to inspect registered providers, models, readiness, and auth hints. Generated images are delivered automatically from the tool result as MEDIA paths.

action.description: Optional action: "generate" (default) or "list" to inspect available providers/models.

image.description: Optional reference image path or URL for edit mode.

images.description: Optional reference images for edit mode (up to 5).

model.description: Optional provider/model override, e.g. openai/gpt-image-2; use openai/gpt-image-1.5 for transparent OpenAI backgrounds.

filename.description: Optional output filename hint. OpenClaw preserves the basename and saves under its managed media directory.

resolution.description: Optional resolution hint: 1K, 2K, or 4K. Useful for Google edit/generation flows.

quality.description: Optional quality hint: low, medium, high, or auto when the provider supports it.

outputFormat.description: Optional output format hint: png, jpeg, or webp when the provider supports it.

background.description: Optional background hint: transparent, opaque, or auto when the provider supports it. For transparent output use outputFormat png or webp.

count.description: Optional number of images to request (1-4).

timeoutMs.description: Optional provider request timeout in milliseconds.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. Optional `corpus=wiki` or `corpus=all` also searches registered compiled-wiki supplements. `corpus=memory` restricts hits to indexed memory files (excludes session transcript chunks from ranking). `corpus=sessions` restricts hits to indexed session transcripts (same visibility rules as session history tools). If response has disabled=true, memory retrieval is unavailable and should be surfaced to the user.

tools.name: music_generate
tools.description: Generate music using configured providers. Generated tracks are saved under OpenClaw-managed media storage and delivered automatically as attachments.

action.description: Optional action: "generate" (default), "status" to inspect the active session task, or "list" to inspect available providers/models.

lyrics.description: Optional lyrics to guide sung output when the provider supports it.

instrumental.description: Optional toggle for instrumental-only output when the provider supports it.

image.description: Optional single reference image path or URL.

images.description: Optional reference images (up to 10).

durationSeconds.description: Optional target duration in seconds when the provider supports duration hints.

timeoutMs.description: Optional provider request timeout in milliseconds. Values below 10000ms are raised to 10000ms.

format.description: Optional output format hint: "mp3" or "wav" when the provider supports it.

filename.description: Optional output filename hint. OpenClaw preserves the basename and saves under its managed media directory.

tools.name: process
tools.description: Manage running exec sessions for commands already started: list, poll, log, write, send-keys, submit, paste, kill. Use poll/log when you need status, logs, quiet-success confirmation, or completion confirmation when automatic completion wake is unavailable. Use write/send-keys/submit/paste/kill for input or intervention. Do not use process polling to emulate timers or reminders; use cron for scheduled follow-ups.

action.description: Process action

sessionId.description: Session id for actions other than list

keys.description: Key tokens to send for send-keys

hex.description: Hex bytes to send for send-keys

offset.description: Log offset

limit.description: Log length

timeout.description: For poll: wait up to this many milliseconds before returning; max 30000 ms, higher values are clamped to 30000

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: session_status
tools.description: Show a /status-equivalent session status card for the current or another visible session, including usage, time, cost when available, and linked background task context. Use `sessionKey="current"` for the current session; do not use UI/client labels such as `openclaw-tui` as session keys. Optional `model` sets a per-session model override; `model=default` resets overrides. Use this for questions like what model is active or how a session is configured.

tools.name: sessions_history
tools.description: Fetch sanitized message history for a visible session. Supports limits and optional tool messages; use this to inspect another session before replying, debugging, or resuming work.

tools.name: sessions_list
tools.description: List visible sessions with optional filters for kind, label, agentId, search, recent activity, derived titles, and last-message previews. Use this to discover a target session before calling sessions_history or sessions_send.

tools.name: sessions_send
tools.description: Send a message into another visible session by sessionKey or label. Thread-scoped chat sessions are rejected; target the parent channel session for inter-agent coordination. Use this to delegate follow-up work to an existing session; waits for the target run and returns the updated assistant reply when available.

tools.name: sessions_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a clean isolated session by default with the native subagent runtime. `mode="run"` is one-shot background work. Subagents inherit the parent workspace directory automatically. For native subagents only, set `context="fork"` when the child needs the current transcript context; otherwise omit it or use `context="isolated"`. Use this when the work should happen in a fresh child session instead of the current one.

context.description: Native subagent context mode. Omit or use "isolated" for a clean child session; use "fork" only when the child needs the requester transcript context.

lightContext.description: When true, spawned subagent runs use lightweight bootstrap context. Only applies to runtime='subagent'.

tools.name: sessions_yield
tools.description: End your current turn. Use after spawning subagents to receive their results as the next message.

tools.name: subagents
tools.description: List, kill, or steer spawned sub-agents for this requester session. Use this for sub-agent orchestration.

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Update the current structured work plan for this run. Use this for non-trivial multi-step work so the plan stays current while execution continues. Keep steps short, mark at most one step as `in_progress`, and skip this tool for simple one-step tasks.

explanation.description: Optional short note explaining what changed in the plan.

plan.description: Ordered list of plan steps. At most one step may be in_progress.

tools.name: video_generate
tools.description: Generate videos using configured providers. Generated videos are saved under OpenClaw-managed media storage and delivered automatically as attachments. Duration requests may be rounded to the nearest provider-supported value.

action.description: Optional action: "generate" (default), "status" to inspect the active session task, or "list" to inspect available providers/models.

image.description: Optional single reference image path or URL.

images.description: Optional reference images (up to 9).

imageRoles.description: Optional semantic roles for the combined reference image list, parallel by index. The list is `image` (if provided) followed by each entry in `images`, in order, after de-duplication. Canonical values: "first_frame", "last_frame", "reference_image". Providers may accept additional role strings. Must not have more entries than the combined image list; use an empty string to leave a position unset.

video.description: Optional single reference video path or URL.

videoRoles.description: Optional semantic roles for the combined reference video list, parallel by index. The list is `video` (if provided) followed by each entry in `videos`, in order, after de-duplication. Canonical value: "reference_video". Providers may accept additional role strings. Must not have more entries than the combined video list; use an empty string to leave a position unset.

audioRef.description: Optional single reference audio path or URL (e.g. background music).

audioRoles.description: Optional semantic roles for the combined reference audio list, parallel by index. The list is `audioRef` (if provided) followed by each entry in `audioRefs`, in order, after de-duplication. Canonical value: "reference_audio". Providers may accept additional role strings. Must not have more entries than the combined audio list; use an empty string to leave a position unset.

filename.description: Optional output filename hint. OpenClaw preserves the basename and saves under its managed media directory.

size.description: Optional size hint like 1280x720 or 1920x1080 when the provider supports it.

aspectRatio.description: Optional aspect ratio hint such as 1:1, 16:9, 9:16, "adaptive", or a provider-specific value. OpenClaw normalizes or ignores unsupported values per provider.

resolution.description: Optional resolution hint such as 480P, 720P, 768P, 1080P, 4K, or a provider-specific value. OpenClaw normalizes or ignores unsupported values per provider.

durationSeconds.description: Optional target duration in seconds. OpenClaw may round this to the nearest provider-supported duration.

audio.description: Optional audio toggle when the provider supports generated audio.

watermark.description: Optional watermark toggle when the provider supports it.

providerOptions.description: Optional provider-specific options as a JSON object, e.g. `{"seed": 42, "draft": true}`. Each provider declares its own accepted keys and primitive types (number/boolean/string) via its capabilities; unknown keys or type mismatches skip the candidate during fallback and never silently reach the wrong provider. Run `video_generate action=list` to see which keys each provider accepts.

timeoutMs.description: Optional provider request timeout in milliseconds.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

assistantTexts: Bon dia, Albert. Me pongo con ello como MVP: guardaré cada lectura con fecha/hora y la mostraré en el Dashboard Salud con una gráfica sencilla.

Hecho, Albert ✅

Añadí al **Dashboard Salud**:

- Formulario para introducir:
  - Tensión sistólica
  - Tensión diastólica
  - Pulso opcional
  - Fecha y hora de introducción
- Gráfica simple con línea de sistólica y diastólica.
- Tabla con el histórico de lecturas.
- Guardado privado en el navegador usando `localStorage`.
- Botón para **exportar JSON** como copia de seguridad.
- Documentación actualizada en `dashboard/README.md`.

Verificado:
- El dashboard carga por HTTP local correctamente.
- El JavaScript pasa comprobación de sintaxis.

Nota importante: como el dashboard sigue siendo estático y seguro, los datos quedan guardados en ese navegador/dispositivo. La siguiente iteración podría ser guardar también en archivo local del workspace, pero eso ya requiere un pequeño backend/local service.

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`
- Current values are estimated from `session_status` snapshots, not exact per-task accounting.
- Channels are grouped as Telegram, TUI, automations, subagents, or unknown.
- Visual bars are static CSS, with no external libraries or network calls.

Stability MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Phase 1 is observe-only: no automatic gateway restarts, no tool freezing, no external alerts.
- Shows uptime, RAM, CPU load, approximate tokens/hour, critical errors, loops, confirmed gateway restarts, anomalous consumption, and a daily stability score.

Tools/plugins audit MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Read-only inventory: plugins discovered/loaded/disabled, plugin doctor status, eligible skills, active automations, and prudential warnings.
- No plugin/tool is disabled from the dashboard; changes require explicit Albert approval.

Quick launcher:
- Script: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/open-dashboard.sh`
- Desktop entry: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/neodaemon-dashboard.desktop`
- The launcher starts a local-only server on `127.0.0.1:8765` and opens the dashboard in the browser.

Open `index.html` locally when explicitly approved/needed.

- Albert propuso una línea futura de observabilidad/estabilidad, insistiendo en “NO más complejidad”: watchdog gateway, snapshots nocturnos, panel de salud sistema, detector de loops, clasificación automática del log diario, modo mantenimiento, auditoría de tools y score diario de estabilidad.
- Tras aprobación de Albert, se implementó solo fase 1 de observabilidad: MVP local de salud/estabilidad en modo observación, sin reinicios automáticos ni servicios externos. Fuente `/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`; dashboard muestra score, uptime, RAM, CPU, tokens/hora, errores críticos, loops, reinicios y consumo anómalo.
- Albert pidió crear un protocolo previo y seguro para que neodaemon tenga acceso a Internet. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md` con niveles de permiso, coste 0€, privacidad por defecto, lectura antes que acción, y aprobación obligatoria para acciones externas.
- Albert envió un PDF con un protocolo más estricto previo a dar acceso a Internet a OpenClaw. Se fusionó en `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md`: fase 0 con requisitos previos, política de solo lectura inicial, sandboxing, observabilidad obligatoria, human-in-the-loop, allowlist, rate limiting, modo observación 7–14 días y sistema de emergencia.
- Albert indicó que tiene hosting web, dominio propio y quiere acceder al dashboard desde fuera de casa. Recomendación pendiente: empezar con dashboard estático solo lectura protegido, sin exponer OpenClaw ni herramientas internas.
- Se creó una alerta cron cada 30 minutos para revisar el consumo diario de tokens de la sesión principal de Telegram y avisar a Albert si el consumo alcanza >=95% (<=5% libre). Job: `alerta-consumo-tokens-diario-95`. Tras detectar bloqueos de visibilidad desde sesión aislada, se ajustó a `sessionTarget=current` y `session_status(sessionKey="current")`. Luego Albert pidió evitar actividad no urgente de 22:00 a 08:00 para ahorrar tokens/ruido; inicialmente quedó cada 30 min en horario diurno, y después Albert lo redujo a una vez por hora con `0 8-21 * * *` Europe/Madrid.
- Albert confirmó como principio rector: “Orden, rigor y seguridad”. La regla queda fijada: primero ordenar, luego medir, después automatizar solo lo seguro.
- Albert indicó que ha creado un correo propio e individual de Gmail para neodaemon. No guardar credenciales en memoria ni en chats; usarlo solo tras definir protocolo seguro de acceso/uso.
- Albert aprobó auditar tools/plugins tras revisar el core. Se hizo auditoría solo lectura y se guardó en `/personal/albert/auditoria-tools-plugins-2026-05-10.md`: 92 plugins descubiertos, 67 loaded, 25 disabled, plugin doctor limpio, 7 skills elegibles, 3 cron activos, y advertencias de seguridad sobre allowlist de grupos Telegram, trusted proxies si se expone gateway, y modelo de confianza personal/no multiusuario.
- Se añadió al dashboard un panel read-only “Tools / plugins” con fuente `/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`, mostrando inventario, estado plugin doctor, skills elegibles, automatizaciones activas y advertencias; sin desactivar nada.
- Albert propuso trabajar `MEMORY.md` como memoria curada y hacer auditorías generales/core cada 15 días. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-auditoria-quincenal.md` y cron `auditoria-quincenal-core-general`, primera ejecución 2026-05-25 10:00 Europe/Madrid, modo solo lectura, sin Internet, sin secretos ni cambios automáticos.
- Albert refinó la estrategia de backups: el objetivo real es capacidad fiable de recuperación, no solo tener backups. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-backups-recuperacion.md` con restore verification mensual en VM aislada, clasificación A/B/C por sensibilidad, golden snapshot, política anti-corrupción, retención 7 diarios/4 semanales/3 mensuales, checksums SHA256/manifest, y snapshot manual verificado antes de Internet/plugins/tools/multiagentes/automatizaciones.

tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description: Apply a patch to one or more files using the apply_patch format. The input should include *** Begin Patch and *** End Patch markers.

tools.name: cron
tools.description:
Manage Gateway cron jobs (status/list/add/update/remove/run/runs) and send wake events. Use this for reminders, "check back later" requests, delayed follow-ups, and recurring tasks. Do not emulate scheduling with exec sleep or process polling.

Main-session cron jobs enqueue system events for heartbeat handling. Isolated cron jobs create background task runs that appear in `openclaw tasks`.

ACTIONS:
- status: Check cron scheduler status
- list: List jobs (use includeDisabled:true to include disabled)
- add: Create job (requires job object, see schema below)
- update: Modify job (requires jobId + patch object)
- remove: Delete job (requires jobId)
- run: Trigger job immediately (requires jobId)
- runs: Get job run history (requires jobId)
- wake: Send wake event (requires text, optional mode)

JOB SCHEMA (for add action):
{
  "name": "string (optional)",
  "schedule": { ... },      // Required: when to run
  "payload": { ... },       // Required: what to execute
  "delivery": { ... },      // Optional: announce summary (isolated/current/session:xxx only) or webhook POST
  "sessionTarget": "main" | "isolated" | "current" | "session:<custom-id>",  // Optional, defaults based on context
  "enabled": true | false   // Optional, default true
}

SESSION TARGET OPTIONS:
- "main": Run in the main session (requires payload.kind="systemEvent")
- "isolated": Run in an ephemeral isolated session (requires payload.kind="agentTurn")
- "current": Bind to the current session where the cron is created (resolved at creation time)
- "session:<custom-id>": Run in a persistent named session (e.g., "session:project-alpha-daily")

DEFAULT BEHAVIOR (unchanged for backward compatibility):
- payload.kind="systemEvent" → defaults to "main"
- payload.kind="agentTurn" → defaults to "isolated"
To use current session binding, explicitly set sessionTarget="current".

SCHEDULE TYPES (schedule.kind):
- "at": One-shot at absolute time
  { "kind": "at", "at": "<ISO-8601 timestamp>" }
- "every": Recurring interval
  { "kind": "every", "everyMs": <interval-ms>, "anchorMs": <optional-start-ms> }
- "cron": Cron expression evaluated in the supplied timezone, or the Gateway host local timezone when tz is omitted
  { "kind": "cron", "expr": "<cron-expression>", "tz": "<optional-IANA-timezone>" }
  Write expr in the selected timezone's local wall-clock time; do not convert the requested local time to UTC first.
  If tz is omitted, do not assume UTC; the Gateway host local timezone is used.
  Example: "Remind me every day at 6pm Shanghai time" -> { "kind": "cron", "expr": "0 18 * * *", "tz": "Asia/Shanghai" }

For schedule.kind="at", ISO timestamps without an explicit timezone are treated as UTC.

PAYLOAD TYPES (payload.kind):
- "systemEvent": Injects text as system event into session
  { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "<message>" }
- "agentTurn": Runs agent with message (isolated sessions only)
  { "kind": "agentTurn", "message": "<prompt>", "model": "<optional>", "thinking": "<optional>", "timeoutSeconds": <optional, 0 means no timeout> }

DELIVERY (top-level):
  { "mode": "none|announce|webhook", "channel": "<optional>", "to": "<optional>", "threadId": "<optional>", "bestEffort": <optional-bool> }
  - Default for isolated agentTurn jobs (when delivery omitted): "announce"
  - announce: send to chat channel (optional channel/to target)
  - threadId: chat thread/topic id for channels that support threaded delivery
  - webhook: send finished-run event as HTTP POST to delivery.to (URL required)
  - If the task needs to send to a specific chat/recipient, set announce delivery.channel/to; do not call messaging tools inside the run.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
- sessionTarget="main" REQUIRES payload.kind="systemEvent"
- sessionTarget="isolated" | "current" | "session:xxx" REQUIRES payload.kind="agentTurn"
- For webhook callbacks, use delivery.mode="webhook" with delivery.to set to a URL.
Default: prefer isolated agentTurn jobs unless the user explicitly wants current-session binding.

WAKE MODES (for wake action):
- "next-heartbeat" (default): Wake on next heartbeat
- "now": Wake immediately

Use jobId as the canonical identifier; id is accepted for compatibility. Use contextMessages (0-10) to add previous messages as context to the job text.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: exec
tools.description: Execute shell commands with background continuation for work that starts now. Use yieldMs/background to continue later via process tool. For long-running work started now, rely on automatic completion wake when it is enabled and the command emits output or fails; otherwise use process to confirm completion. Use process whenever you need logs, status, input, or intervention. Do not use exec sleep or delay loops for reminders or deferred follow-ups; use cron instead. Use pty=true for TTY-required commands (terminal UIs, coding agents).

background.description: Run in background immediately

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, kills process on expiry)

pty.description: Run in a pseudo-terminal (PTY) when available (TTY-required CLIs, coding agents)

tools.name: image_generate
tools.description: Generate new images or edit reference images with the configured or inferred image-generation model. Set agents.defaults.imageGenerationModel.primary to pick a provider/model. Providers declare their own auth/readiness; use action="list" to inspect registered providers, models, readiness, and auth hints. Generated images are delivered automatically from the tool result as MEDIA paths.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. Optional `corpus=wiki` or `corpus=all` also searches registered compiled-wiki supplements. `corpus=memory` restricts hits to indexed memory files (excludes session transcript chunks from ranking). `corpus=sessions` restricts hits to indexed session transcripts (same visibility rules as session history tools). tools.name: music_generate
tools.description: Generate music using configured providers. Generated tracks are saved under OpenClaw-managed media storage and delivered automatically as attachments.

tools.name: process
tools.description: Manage running exec sessions for commands already started: list, poll, log, write, send-keys, submit, paste, kill. Use poll/log when you need status, logs, quiet-success confirmation, or completion confirmation when automatic completion wake is unavailable. Use write/send-keys/submit/paste/kill for input or intervention. Do not use process polling to emulate timers or reminders; use cron for scheduled follow-ups.

tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

tools.name: session_status
tools.description: Show a /status-equivalent session status card for the current or another visible session, including usage, time, cost when available, and linked background task context. Use `sessionKey="current"` for the current session; do not use UI/client labels such as `openclaw-tui` as session keys. Optional `model` sets a per-session model override; `model=default` resets overrides. Use this for questions like what model is active or how a session is configured.

tools.name: sessions_history
tools.description: Fetch sanitized message history for a visible session. Supports limits and optional tool messages; use this to inspect another session before replying, debugging, or resuming work.

tools.name: sessions_list
tools.description: List visible sessions with optional filters for kind, label, agentId, search, recent activity, derived titles, and last-message previews. Use this to discover a target session before calling sessions_history or sessions_send.

tools.name: sessions_send
tools.description: Send a message into another visible session by sessionKey or label. Thread-scoped chat sessions are rejected; target the parent channel session for inter-agent coordination. Use this to delegate follow-up work to an existing session; waits for the target run and returns the updated assistant reply when available.

tools.name: sessions_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a clean isolated session by default with the native subagent runtime. `mode="run"` is one-shot background work. Subagents inherit the parent workspace directory automatically. For native subagents only, set `context="fork"` when the child needs the current transcript context; otherwise omit it or use `context="isolated"`. Use this when the work should happen in a fresh child session instead of the current one.

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`
- Current values are estimated from `session_status` snapshots, not exact per-task accounting.
- Channels are grouped as Telegram, TUI, automations, subagents, or unknown.
- Visual bars are static CSS, with no external libraries or network calls.

Stability MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Phase 1 is observe-only: no automatic gateway restarts, no tool freezing, no external alerts.
- Shows uptime, RAM, CPU load, approximate tokens/hour, critical errors, loops, confirmed gateway restarts, anomalous consumption, and a daily stability score.

Tools/plugins audit MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Read-only inventory: plugins discovered/loaded/disabled, plugin doctor status, eligible skills, active automations, and prudential warnings.
- No plugin/tool is disabled from the dashboard; changes require explicit Albert approval.

Quick launcher:
- Script: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/open-dashboard.sh`
- Desktop entry: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/neodaemon-dashboard.desktop`
- The launcher starts a local-only server on `127.0.0.1:8765` and opens the dashboard in the browser.

Open `index.html` locally when explicitly approved/needed.

- Albert propuso una línea futura de observabilidad/estabilidad, insistiendo en “NO más complejidad”: watchdog gateway, snapshots nocturnos, panel de salud sistema, detector de loops, clasificación automática del log diario, modo mantenimiento, auditoría de tools y score diario de estabilidad.
- Tras aprobación de Albert, se implementó solo fase 1 de observabilidad: MVP local de salud/estabilidad en modo observación, sin reinicios automáticos ni servicios externos. Fuente `/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`; dashboard muestra score, uptime, RAM, CPU, tokens/hora, errores críticos, loops, reinicios y consumo anómalo.
- Albert pidió crear un protocolo previo y seguro para que neodaemon tenga acceso a Internet. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md` con niveles de permiso, coste 0€, privacidad por defecto, lectura antes que acción, y aprobación obligatoria para acciones externas.
- Albert envió un PDF con un protocolo más estricto previo a dar acceso a Internet a OpenClaw. Se fusionó en `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md`: fase 0 con requisitos previos, política de solo lectura inicial, sandboxing, observabilidad obligatoria, human-in-the-loop, allowlist, rate limiting, modo observación 7–14 días y sistema de emergencia.
- Albert indicó que tiene hosting web, dominio propio y quiere acceder al dashboard desde fuera de casa. Recomendación pendiente: empezar con dashboard estático solo lectura protegido, sin exponer OpenClaw ni herramientas internas.
- Se creó una alerta cron cada 30 minutos para revisar el consumo diario de tokens de la sesión principal de Telegram y avisar a Albert si el consumo alcanza >=95% (<=5% libre). Job: `alerta-consumo-tokens-diario-95`. Tras detectar bloqueos de visibilidad desde sesión aislada, se ajustó a `sessionTarget=current` y `session_status(sessionKey="current")`. Luego Albert pidió evitar actividad no urgente de 22:00 a 08:00 para ahorrar tokens/ruido; inicialmente quedó cada 30 min en horario diurno, y después Albert lo redujo a una vez por hora con `0 8-21 * * *` Europe/Madrid.
- Albert confirmó como principio rector: “Orden, rigor y seguridad”. La regla queda fijada: primero ordenar, luego medir, después automatizar solo lo seguro.
- Albert indicó que ha creado un correo propio e individual de Gmail para neodaemon. No guardar credenciales en memoria ni en chats; usarlo solo tras definir protocolo seguro de acceso/uso.
- Albert aprobó auditar tools/plugins tras revisar el core. Se hizo auditoría solo lectura y se guardó en `/personal/albert/auditoria-tools-plugins-2026-05-10.md`: 92 plugins descubiertos, 67 loaded, 25 disabled, plugin doctor limpio, 7 skills elegibles, 3 cron activos, y advertencias de seguridad sobre allowlist de grupos Telegram, trusted proxies si se expone gateway, y modelo de confianza personal/no multiusuario.
- Se añadió al dashboard un panel read-only “Tools / plugins” con fuente `/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`, mostrando inventario, estado plugin doctor, skills elegibles, automatizaciones activas y advertencias; sin desactivar nada.
- Albert propuso trabajar `MEMORY.md` como memoria curada y hacer auditorías generales/core cada 15 días. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-auditoria-quincenal.md` y cron `auditoria-quincenal-core-general`, primera ejecución 2026-05-25 10:00 Europe/Madrid, modo solo lectura, sin Internet, sin secretos ni cambios automáticos.
- Albert refinó la estrategia de backups: el objetivo real es capacidad fiable de recuperación, no solo tener backups. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-backups-recuperacion.md` con restore verification mensual en VM aislada, clasificación A/B/C por sensibilidad, golden snapshot, política anti-corrupción, retención 7 diarios/4 semanales/3 mensuales, checksums SHA256/manifest, y snapshot manual verificado antes de Internet/plugins/tools/multiagentes/automatizaciones.

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`
- Current values are estimated from `session_status` snapshots, not exact per-task accounting.
- Channels are grouped as Telegram, TUI, automations, subagents, or unknown.
- Visual bars are static CSS, with no external libraries or network calls.

Stability MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Phase 1 is observe-only: no automatic gateway restarts, no tool freezing, no external alerts.
- Shows uptime, RAM, CPU load, approximate tokens/hour, critical errors, loops, confirmed gateway restarts, anomalous consumption, and a daily stability score.

Tools/plugins audit MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Read-only inventory: plugins discovered/loaded/disabled, plugin doctor status, eligible skills, active automations, and prudential warnings.
- No plugin/tool is disabled from the dashboard; changes require explicit Albert approval.

Quick launcher:
- Script: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/open-dashboard.sh`
- Desktop entry: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/neodaemon-dashboard.desktop`
- The launcher starts a local-only server on `127.0.0.1:8765` and opens the dashboard in the browser.

Open `index.html` locally when explicitly approved/needed.

- Se añadió al dashboard MVP un bloque manual de uso LLM/tokens con entrada, salida, contexto, cache y límite diario aproximado según `session_status`. Es snapshot manual, no contador en vivo.
- Albert aprobó añadir la métrica “tokens por tarea útil”. Se implementó como MVP local 0€: fuente JSONL en `/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`, cálculo estimado desde snapshots de `session_status`, clasificación por canal y visualización CSS simple en el dashboard.
- Albert propuso una línea futura de observabilidad/estabilidad, insistiendo en “NO más complejidad”: watchdog gateway, snapshots nocturnos, panel de salud sistema, detector de loops, clasificación automática del log diario, modo mantenimiento, auditoría de tools y score diario de estabilidad.
- Tras aprobación de Albert, se implementó solo fase 1 de observabilidad: MVP local de salud/estabilidad en modo observación, sin reinicios automáticos ni servicios externos. Fuente `/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`; dashboard muestra score, uptime, RAM, CPU, tokens/hora, errores críticos, loops, reinicios y consumo anómalo.
- Albert pidió crear un protocolo previo y seguro para que neodaemon tenga acceso a Internet. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md` con niveles de permiso, coste 0€, privacidad por defecto, lectura antes que acción, y aprobación obligatoria para acciones externas.
- Albert envió un PDF con un protocolo más estricto previo a dar acceso a Internet a OpenClaw. Se fusionó en `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md`: fase 0 con requisitos previos, política de solo lectura inicial, sandboxing, observabilidad obligatoria, human-in-the-loop, allowlist, rate limiting, modo observación 7–14 días y sistema de emergencia.
- Albert indicó que tiene hosting web, dominio propio y quiere acceder al dashboard desde fuera de casa. Recomendación pendiente: empezar con dashboard estático solo lectura protegido, sin exponer OpenClaw ni herramientas internas.
- Se creó una alerta cron cada 30 minutos para revisar el consumo diario de tokens de la sesión principal de Telegram y avisar a Albert si el consumo alcanza >=95% (<=5% libre). Job: `alerta-consumo-tokens-diario-95`. Tras detectar bloqueos de visibilidad desde sesión aislada, se ajustó a `sessionTarget=current` y `session_status(sessionKey="current")`. Luego Albert pidió evitar actividad no urgente de 22:00 a 08:00 para ahorrar tokens/ruido; inicialmente quedó cada 30 min en horario diurno, y después Albert lo redujo a una vez por hora con `0 8-21 * * *` Europe/Madrid.
- Albert confirmó como principio rector: “Orden, rigor y seguridad”. La regla queda fijada: primero ordenar, luego medir, después automatizar solo lo seguro.
- Albert indicó que ha creado un correo propio e individual de Gmail para neodaemon. No guardar credenciales en memoria ni en chats; usarlo solo tras definir protocolo seguro de acceso/uso.
- Albert aprobó auditar tools/plugins tras revisar el core. Se hizo auditoría solo lectura y se guardó en `/personal/albert/auditoria-tools-plugins-2026-05-10.md`: 92 plugins descubiertos, 67 loaded, 25 disabled, plugin doctor limpio, 7 skills elegibles, 3 cron activos, y advertencias de seguridad sobre allowlist de grupos Telegram, trusted proxies si se expone gateway, y modelo de confianza personal/no multiusuario.
- Se añadió al dashboard un panel read-only “Tools / plugins” con fuente `/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`, mostrando inventario, estado plugin doctor, skills elegibles, automatizaciones activas y advertencias; sin desactivar nada.
- Albert propuso trabajar `MEMORY.md` como memoria curada y hacer auditorías generales/core cada 15 días. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-auditoria-quincenal.md` y cron `auditoria-quincenal-core-general`, primera ejecución 2026-05-25 10:00 Europe/Madrid, modo solo lectura, sin Internet, sin secretos ni cambios automáticos.
- Albert refinó la estrategia de backups: el objetivo real es capacidad fiable de recuperación, no solo tener backups. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-backups-recuperacion.md` con restore verification mensual en VM aislada, clasificación A/B/C por sensibilidad, golden snapshot, política anti-corrupción, retención 7 diarios/4 semanales/3 mensuales, checksums SHA256/manifest, y snapshot manual verificado antes de Internet/plugins/tools/multiagentes/automatizaciones.
- Albert preguntó si activar backups automáticos. Se activó solo backup ligero operativo/histórico (niveles B/C), no el backup completo sensible A. Script: `/personal/albert/scripts/backup-ligero-operativo.sh`; salida en `/backups/operational/YYYY/MM/DD/`; verificación tar + SHA256; retención MVP de 7 diarios; cron diario 10:15 Europe/Madrid `backup-ligero-operativo-diario`. Se ejecutó un primer backup verificado OK.

# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`

- Se añadió al dashboard MVP un bloque manual de uso LLM/tokens con entrada, salida, contexto, cache y límite diario aproximado según `session_status`. Es snapshot manual, no contador en vivo.
- Albert aprobó añadir la métrica “tokens por tarea útil”. Se implementó como MVP local 0€: fuente JSONL en `/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`, cálculo estimado desde snapshots de `session_status`, clasificación por canal y visualización CSS simple en el dashboard.
- Albert propuso una línea futura de observabilidad/estabilidad, insistiendo en “NO más complejidad”: watchdog gateway, snapshots nocturnos, panel de salud sistema, detector de loops, clasificación automática del log diario, modo mantenimiento, auditoría de tools y score diario de estabilidad.
- Tras aprobación de Albert, se implementó solo fase 1 de observabilidad: MVP local de salud/estabilidad en modo observación, sin reinicios automáticos ni servicios externos. Fuente `/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`; dashboard muestra score, uptime, RAM, CPU, tokens/hora, errores críticos, loops, reinicios y consumo anómalo.
- Albert pidió crear un protocolo previo y seguro para que neodaemon tenga acceso a Internet. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md` con niveles de permiso, coste 0€, privacidad por defecto, lectura antes que acción, y aprobación obligatoria para acciones externas.
- Albert envió un PDF con un protocolo más estricto previo a dar acceso a Internet a OpenClaw. Se fusionó en `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md`: fase 0 con requisitos previos, política de solo lectura inicial, sandboxing, observabilidad obligatoria, human-in-the-loop, allowlist, rate limiting, modo observación 7–14 días y sistema de emergencia.
- Albert indicó que tiene hosting web, dominio propio y quiere acceder al dashboard desde fuera de casa. Recomendación pendiente: empezar con dashboard estático solo lectura protegido, sin exponer OpenClaw ni herramientas internas.
- Se creó una alerta cron cada 30 minutos para revisar el consumo diario de tokens de la sesión principal de Telegram y avisar a Albert si el consumo alcanza >=95% (<=5% libre). Job: `alerta-consumo-tokens-diario-95`. Tras detectar bloqueos de visibilidad desde sesión aislada, se ajustó a `sessionTarget=current` y `session_status(sessionKey="current")`. tools.description: Apply a patch to one or more files using the apply_patch format. The input should include *** Begin Patch and *** End Patch markers.

tools.name: cron
tools.description:
Manage Gateway cron jobs (status/list/add/update/remove/run/runs) and send wake events. Use this for reminders, "check back later" requests, delayed follow-ups, and recurring tasks. Do not emulate scheduling with exec sleep or process polling.

Main-session cron jobs enqueue system events for heartbeat handling. Isolated cron jobs create background task runs that appear in `openclaw tasks`.

ACTIONS:
- status: Check cron scheduler status
- list: List jobs (use includeDisabled:true to include disabled)
- add: Create job (requires job object, see schema below)
- update: Modify job (requires jobId + patch object)
- remove: Delete job (requires jobId)
- run: Trigger job immediately (requires jobId)
- runs: Get job run history (requires jobId)
- wake: Send wake event (requires text, optional mode)

JOB SCHEMA (for add action):
{
  "name": "string (optional)",
  "schedule": { ... },      // Required: when to run
  "payload": { ... },       // Required: what to execute
  "delivery": { ... },      // Optional: announce summary (isolated/current/session:xxx only) or webhook POST
  "sessionTarget": "main" | "isolated" | "current" | "session:<custom-id>",  // Optional, defaults based on context
  "enabled": true | false   // Optional, default true
}

SESSION TARGET OPTIONS:
- "main": Run in the main session (requires payload.kind="systemEvent")
- "isolated": Run in an ephemeral isolated session (requires payload.kind="agentTurn")
- "current": Bind to the current session where the cron is created (resolved at creation time)
- "session:<custom-id>": Run in a persistent named session (e.g., "session:project-alpha-daily")

DEFAULT BEHAVIOR (unchanged for backward compatibility):
- payload.kind="systemEvent" → defaults to "main"
- payload.kind="agentTurn" → defaults to "isolated"
To use current session binding, explicitly set sessionTarget="current".

SCHEDULE TYPES (schedule.kind):
- "at": One-shot at absolute time
  { "kind": "at", "at": "<ISO-8601 timestamp>" }
- "every": Recurring interval
  { "kind": "every", "everyMs": <interval-ms>, "anchorMs": <optional-start-ms> }
- "cron": Cron expression evaluated in the supplied timezone, or the Gateway host local timezone when tz is omitted
  { "kind": "cron", "expr": "<cron-expression>", "tz": "<optional-IANA-timezone>" }
  Write expr in the selected timezone's local wall-clock time; do not convert the requested local time to UTC first.
  If tz is omitted, do not assume UTC; the Gateway host local timezone is used.
  Example: "Remind me every day at 6pm Shanghai time" -> { "kind": "cron", "expr": "0 18 * * *", "tz": "Asia/Shanghai" }

For schedule.kind="at", ISO timestamps without an explicit timezone are treated as UTC.

PAYLOAD TYPES (payload.kind):
- "systemEvent": Injects text as system event into session
  { "kind": "systemEvent", "text": "<message>" }
- "agentTurn": Runs agent with message (isolated sessions only)
  { "kind": "agentTurn", "message": "<prompt>", "model": "<optional>", "thinking": "<optional>", "timeoutSeconds": <optional, 0 means no timeout> }

DELIVERY (top-level):
  { "mode": "none|announce|webhook", "channel": "<optional>", "to": "<optional>", "threadId": "<optional>", "bestEffort": <optional-bool> }
  - Default for isolated agentTurn jobs (when delivery omitted): "announce"
  - announce: send to chat channel (optional channel/to target)
  - threadId: chat thread/topic id for channels that support threaded delivery
  - webhook: send finished-run event as HTTP POST to delivery.to (URL required)
  - If the task needs to send to a specific chat/recipient, set announce delivery.channel/to; do not call messaging tools inside the run.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINTS:
- sessionTarget="main" REQUIRES payload.kind="systemEvent"
- sessionTarget="isolated" | "current" | "session:xxx" REQUIRES payload.kind="agentTurn"
- For webhook callbacks, use delivery.mode="webhook" with delivery.to set to a URL.
Default: prefer isolated agentTurn jobs unless the user explicitly wants current-session binding.

WAKE MODES (for wake action):
- "next-heartbeat" (default): Wake on next heartbeat
- "now": Wake immediately

Use jobId as the canonical identifier; id is accepted for compatibility. Use contextMessages (0-10) to add previous messages as context to the job text.

tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`
- Current values are estimated from `session_status` snapshots, not exact per-task accounting.
- Channels are grouped as Telegram, TUI, automations, subagents, or unknown.
- Visual bars are static CSS, with no external libraries or network calls.

Stability MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Phase 1 is observe-only: no automatic gateway restarts, no tool freezing, no external alerts.
- Shows uptime, RAM, CPU load, approximate tokens/hour, critical errors, loops, confirmed gateway restarts, anomalous consumption, and a daily stability score.

Tools/plugins audit MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Read-only inventory: plugins discovered/loaded/disabled, plugin doctor status, eligible skills, active automations, and prudential warnings.
- No plugin/tool is disabled from the dashboard; changes require explicit Albert approval.

Quick launcher:
- Script: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/open-dashboard.sh`
- Desktop entry: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/neodaemon-dashboard.desktop`
- The launcher starts a local-only server on `127.0.0.1:8765` and opens the dashboard in the browser.

Open `index.html` locally when explicitly approved/needed.

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`
- Current values are estimated from `session_status` snapshots, not exact per-task accounting.
- Channels are grouped as Telegram, TUI, automations, subagents, or unknown.
- Visual bars are static CSS, with no external libraries or network calls.

Stability MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Phase 1 is observe-only: no automatic gateway restarts, no tool freezing, no external alerts.
- Shows uptime, RAM, CPU load, approximate tokens/hour, critical errors, loops, confirmed gateway restarts, anomalous consumption, and a daily stability score.

Tools/plugins audit MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Read-only inventory: plugins discovered/loaded/disabled, plugin doctor status, eligible skills, active automations, and prudential warnings.
- No plugin/tool is disabled from the dashboard; changes require explicit Albert approval.

Quick launcher:
- Script: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/open-dashboard.sh`
- Desktop entry: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/neodaemon-dashboard.desktop`
- The launcher starts a local-only server on `127.0.0.1:8765` and opens the dashboard in the browser.

Open `index.html` locally when explicitly approved/needed.

- Albert propuso una línea futura de observabilidad/estabilidad, insistiendo en “NO más complejidad”: watchdog gateway, snapshots nocturnos, panel de salud sistema, detector de loops, clasificación automática del log diario, modo mantenimiento, auditoría de tools y score diario de estabilidad.
- Tras aprobación de Albert, se implementó solo fase 1 de observabilidad: MVP local de salud/estabilidad en modo observación, sin reinicios automáticos ni servicios externos. Fuente `/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`; dashboard muestra score, uptime, RAM, CPU, tokens/hora, errores críticos, loops, reinicios y consumo anómalo.
- Albert pidió crear un protocolo previo y seguro para que neodaemon tenga acceso a Internet. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md` con niveles de permiso, coste 0€, privacidad por defecto, lectura antes que acción, y aprobación obligatoria para acciones externas.
- Albert envió un PDF con un protocolo más estricto previo a dar acceso a Internet a OpenClaw. Se fusionó en `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md`: fase 0 con requisitos previos, política de solo lectura inicial, sandboxing, observabilidad obligatoria, human-in-the-loop, allowlist, rate limiting, modo observación 7–14 días y sistema de emergencia.
- Albert indicó que tiene hosting web, dominio propio y quiere acceder al dashboard desde fuera de casa. Recomendación pendiente: empezar con dashboard estático solo lectura protegido, sin exponer OpenClaw ni herramientas internas.
- Se creó una alerta cron cada 30 minutos para revisar el consumo diario de tokens de la sesión principal de Telegram y avisar a Albert si el consumo alcanza >=95% (<=5% libre). Job: `alerta-consumo-tokens-diario-95`. Tras detectar bloqueos de visibilidad desde sesión aislada, se ajustó a `sessionTarget=current` y `session_status(sessionKey="current")`. Luego Albert pidió evitar actividad no urgente de 22:00 a 08:00 para ahorrar tokens/ruido; inicialmente quedó cada 30 min en horario diurno, y después Albert lo redujo a una vez por hora con `0 8-21 * * *` Europe/Madrid.

- Albert indicó que ha creado un correo propio e individual de Gmail para neodaemon. No guardar credenciales en memoria ni en chats; usarlo solo tras definir protocolo seguro de acceso/uso.
- Albert aprobó auditar tools/plugins tras revisar el core. Se hizo auditoría solo lectura y se guardó en `/personal/albert/auditoria-tools-plugins-2026-05-10.md`: 92 plugins descubiertos, 67 loaded, 25 disabled, plugin doctor limpio, 7 skills elegibles, 3 cron activos, y advertencias de seguridad sobre allowlist de grupos Telegram, trusted proxies si se expone gateway, y modelo de confianza personal/no multiusuario.

content.text:
# Dashboard MVP

Local, static, read-only dashboard concept for Albert and neodaemon.

Security principles:
- Local files only for now.
- No public exposure.
- No network service started automatically.
- No credentials or secrets stored here.
- MVP first, iterate slowly.

Initial blocks:
1. Today
2. Health / mobility
3. Habits
4. Pending / chaos inbox
5. LLM token usage snapshot
6. Token efficiency: “tokens per useful task”
7. System health / stability score
8. Tools / plugins audit

Token efficiency MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/token_efficiency/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl`
- Current values are estimated from `session_status` snapshots, not exact per-task accounting.
- Channels are grouped as Telegram, TUI, automations, subagents, or unknown.
- Visual bars are static CSS, with no external libraries or network calls.

Stability MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Phase 1 is observe-only: no automatic gateway restarts, no tool freezing, no external alerts.
- Shows uptime, RAM, CPU load, approximate tokens/hour, critical errors, loops, confirmed gateway restarts, anomalous consumption, and a daily stability score.

Tools/plugins audit MVP:
- Source: `/openclaw/workspace/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`
- Read-only inventory: plugins discovered/loaded/disabled, plugin doctor status, eligible skills, active automations, and prudential warnings.
- No plugin/tool is disabled from the dashboard; changes require explicit Albert approval.

Quick launcher:
- Script: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/open-dashboard.sh`
- Desktop entry: `/openclaw/workspace/dashboard/neodaemon-dashboard.desktop`
- The launcher starts a local-only server on `127.0.0.1:8765` and opens the dashboard in the browser.

Open `index.html` locally when explicitly approved/needed.

- Albert propuso una línea futura de observabilidad/estabilidad, insistiendo en “NO más complejidad”: watchdog gateway, snapshots nocturnos, panel de salud sistema, detector de loops, clasificación automática del log diario, modo mantenimiento, auditoría de tools y score diario de estabilidad.
- Tras aprobación de Albert, se implementó solo fase 1 de observabilidad: MVP local de salud/estabilidad en modo observación, sin reinicios automáticos ni servicios externos. Fuente `/metrics/stability/YYYY/MM/DD.json`; dashboard muestra score, uptime, RAM, CPU, tokens/hora, errores críticos, loops, reinicios y consumo anómalo.
- Albert pidió crear un protocolo previo y seguro para que neodaemon tenga acceso a Internet. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md` con niveles de permiso, coste 0€, privacidad por defecto, lectura antes que acción, y aprobación obligatoria para acciones externas.
- Albert envió un PDF con un protocolo más estricto previo a dar acceso a Internet a OpenClaw. Se fusionó en `/personal/albert/protocolo-acceso-internet.md`: fase 0 con requisitos previos, política de solo lectura inicial, sandboxing, observabilidad obligatoria, human-in-the-loop, allowlist, rate limiting, modo observación 7–14 días y sistema de emergencia.
- Albert indicó que tiene hosting web, dominio propio y quiere acceder al dashboard desde fuera de casa. Recomendación pendiente: empezar con dashboard estático solo lectura protegido, sin exponer OpenClaw ni herramientas internas.
- Se creó una alerta cron cada 30 minutos para revisar el consumo diario de tokens de la sesión principal de Telegram y avisar a Albert si el consumo alcanza >=95% (<=5% libre). Job: `alerta-consumo-tokens-diario-95`. Tras detectar bloqueos de visibilidad desde sesión aislada, se ajustó a `sessionTarget=current` y `session_status(sessionKey="current")`. Luego Albert pidió evitar actividad no urgente de 22:00 a 08:00 para ahorrar tokens/ruido; inicialmente quedó cada 30 min en horario diurno, y después Albert lo redujo a una vez por hora con `0 8-21 * * *` Europe/Madrid.
- Albert confirmó como principio rector: “Orden, rigor y seguridad”. La regla queda fijada: primero ordenar, luego medir, después automatizar solo lo seguro.
- Albert indicó que ha creado un correo propio e individual de Gmail para neodaemon. No guardar credenciales en memoria ni en chats; usarlo solo tras definir protocolo seguro de acceso/uso.
- Albert aprobó auditar tools/plugins tras revisar el core. Se hizo auditoría solo lectura y se guardó en `/personal/albert/auditoria-tools-plugins-2026-05-10.md`: 92 plugins descubiertos, 67 loaded, 25 disabled, plugin doctor limpio, 7 skills elegibles, 3 cron activos, y advertencias de seguridad sobre allowlist de grupos Telegram, trusted proxies si se expone gateway, y modelo de confianza personal/no multiusuario.
- Se añadió al dashboard un panel read-only “Tools / plugins” con fuente `/metrics/tools_plugins/YYYY/MM/DD.json`, mostrando inventario, estado plugin doctor, skills elegibles, automatizaciones activas y advertencias; sin desactivar nada.
- Albert propuso trabajar `MEMORY.md` como memoria curada y hacer auditorías generales/core cada 15 días. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-auditoria-quincenal.md` y cron `auditoria-quincenal-core-general`, primera ejecución 2026-05-25 10:00 Europe/Madrid, modo solo lectura, sin Internet, sin secretos ni cambios automáticos.
- Albert refinó la estrategia de backups: el objetivo real es capacidad fiable de recuperación, no solo tener backups. Se creó `/personal/albert/protocolo-backups-recuperacion.md` con restore verification mensual en VM aislada, clasificación A/B/C por sensibilidad, golden snapshot, política anti-corrupción, retención 7 diarios/4 semanales/3 mensuales, checksums SHA256/manifest, y snapshot manual verificado antes de Internet/plugins/tools/multiagentes/automatizaciones.
